six_clause_review.actual_formula: BIND(x,H,b,I) AND UpOnset(U,x,H,I_up) AND DownOnset(D,x,H,I_down) AND Partition(I,I_up,I_down)
six_clause_review.positive: One actor/coordinate and two opposed onset event types are explicitly hypothesized; o is oriented reversal, not logical negation. The State|Event tagged interface is declared.
six_clause_review.debt: Partition has no coverage/disjointness/order axioms. U and later U_ext are separately named with no explicit coidentity. The binder creates x,H,b,I under R1; these are paid contextual arguments, not independently identified entities.

six_clause_review.actual_formula: INDEX(r,x) AND Opposite(I_primary,I_other) AND Range(H,I_other,Extend(a)) AND ReturnPath(x,I,b_hi,b_lo) AND H(x,end(I_down))=b_lo
six_clause_review.positive: A generic local index, opposed branch, return-track predicate and lower boundary are stated, with no forced proper star or horizon.
six_clause_review.debt: ReturnPath(x,I,b_hi,b_lo) has no declared relationship to start/end of I, I_down or I_up. I_primary/I_other are not equated with the partition branches. Extend(a) range is not linked to a_outer. The apparent whole-I return does not by itself derive a closed height cycle.

six_clause_review.actual_formula: begin(I_down)=tau_D AND Downward(H,x,I_down) AND end(I_down)=tau_end_down AND At(x,b_lo,tau_end_down)
six_clause_review.positive: Descent phase begins at tau_D and ends at a lower coordinate with end time tau_end_down; this is a coherent explicit conditional physical account.
six_clause_review.debt: Downward is not formally defined through H monotonicity/derivative in this packet. Nevertheless the intended decreasing branch is clear enough for C0 authorship; absence of executable axioms is not a contradiction.

six_clause_review.actual_formula: tau_U=end(I_down) AND UpOnset(U_ext,x,H,I_up,Extend(a)) AND PrimaryTrace(H,r) AND H(x,end(I_up))=b_hi AND Complete(I_down)
six_clause_review.positive: The author explicitly places the subsequent upward onset at tau_U=end(I_down), retains the same indexed coordinate, and gives upper height at end(I_up). Together with the position contribution U_ext@tau_U and R6 this supports the authored descent-then-ascent content.
six_clause_review.debt: UpOnset/I_up beginning is not expanded into a formal interval law. Completion of I_down is consistent with a later ascent; it does not itself generate a second descending phase after that ascent.

six_clause_review.actual_formula: Carry(x,r,I) AND BaseHeight(x,H,C_ref) AND h_low=b_lo AND BoundaryState(b_hi) AND SameReference(r) AND Dist(c,b_lo)=Dist(c,b_hi)=a_outer AND Closed(I)
six_clause_review.positive: Same-reference carrying, complementary upper/lower states and equal distances from a common midpoint are explicit hypotheses. There is no need to identify x as a fixed star to express them.
six_clause_review.concrete_reconciliation_failure: DAR AM position .3G8 contributes CLOSED(I); END(I)=END(I_down_after_up). C5’s bundled formula retains Closed(I) but omits the END equality. I_down_after_up is never introduced, typed, equated with a partition branch, or related to the prior ascent. R5 says the complete formula is the conjunction of word bundles, so the omitted contribution cannot silently disappear.
six_clause_review.classification: A real unbound phase/interface and incomplete clause/contribution reconciliation, not a proved impossible manuscript event.

six_clause_review.positive: Completion and an ordered endpoint pair are expressly assigned to written groups; it is not an unexpressed English closing sentence.
six_clause_review.debt: CompleteHeightCycle and EndpointPair are asserted predicates with no definitions or inference rules. They therefore name the desired whole-cycle result but do not prove it from C1-C5. EndpointPair=(b_hi,b_lo) does not specify whether these are temporal start/end heights, directional phase endpoints or extrema.

cycle_question.core_problem: C1 supplies a two-branch partition; C3/C4 describe descent then ascent. The detailed DAR AM contribution subsequently names I_down_after_up without any binding. The closing complete-cycle/endpoint predicates have no semantics linking them to that phase or to ReturnPath. Consequently a complete consistent traversal/cycle derivation is unavailable in the current packet.
cycle_question.why_not_unsat: Partition, ReturnPath, Closed, CompleteHeightCycle and EndpointPair are not axiomatized tightly enough to force an impossible endpoint order. I_down_after_up’s suggestive name cannot itself be treated as a proved AFTER relation, and EndpointPair cannot silently be interpreted as start/end heights. Missing definitions are not negative observations.
cycle_question.conditional_conflict_only: If an additional contract required exactly two connected ordered phases covering I, descent then ascent, end(I)=end(I_up), and ReturnPath/EndpointPair forced H(x,end(I))=b_lo, C4’s upper endpoint plus b_lo<b_hi would conflict. Those added laws are not currently declared; no such conditional conflict is reported as the frozen candidate’s UNSAT.
cycle_question.no_rescue: This critic neither redefines a branch as disconnected, renames I_down_after_up, identifies it with an existing interval, drops the DAR AM equality, changes EndpointPair to extrema, nor invents a second descent. Any such change requires separate prospective authorship and new costs.
